mappings.note: Case study on a trekking map: reads conventional symbols (triangle peaks, blue rivers) and applies a 1 cm = 1 km scale, which is LO-4, and also asks the bearing to the campsite, which is LO-1. Not LO-3, because the Himalayan setting is only scenery - no Indian physical feature has to be located on a map of India.

Tokyo to San Francisco across the Date Line: the item turns on longitudes 140 E and 122 W and the 180-degree gap (LO-2) and on the date change that the earth's rotation forces (C-SST1.1-LO-3). Not LO-1, since the eastward heading is incidental to the time arithmetic.

Pupils draw their own campus map choosing orientation and symbols - the one item in the chapter that literally matches LO-4's 'draw a neighbourhood map ... with the help of conventional symbols'; LO-1 is added for placing the library east and the playground north.
